title_ar: فضيلة الشيخ الددو يشارك في مؤتمر " دور الجامعات العربية في تعزيز مبدأ الوسطية".
title_en: His Eminence Sheikh al-Dedew Takes Part in the Conference "The Role of Arab Universities in Strengthening the Principle of Balance"
body_ar: شارك فضيلة العلامة الشيخ محمد الحسن ولد الددو -رئيس مركز تكوين العلماء ورئيس جامعة عبد الله بن ياسين في مؤتمر حول " دور الجامعات العربية في تعزيز مبدأ الوسطية بين الشباب العربي" الذي تنظمه جامعة طيبة في فندق الميريديان بالمدينة المنورة، والمنعقد في الفترة ما بين ( 1 – 4) ربيع الثاني 1432 ه الموافق ل ( 6- 9) / 03 / 2011م. وقد شارك في هذا المؤتمر لفيف كبير من علماء العالم الإسلامي وتمثلت مشاركة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو رئيس مركز تكوين العلماء بمحاضرة في الندوة الكبرى بعنوان: " وسطية الإسلام وأثرها في الفكر والسلوك". ومن ضمن المحاضرات والأنشطة التي يقيمها الشيخ داخل أروقة الجامعة؛ دورة خاصة في شرح كتاب "الأخلاق والسير " لابن حزم، وهي الدورة الثانية في مدارسة وشرح هذا الكتاب. كما ألقى فضيلته ضمن الفعاليات المصاحبة للمؤتمر الذي تنظمه الجامعة هذه الأيام محاضرة بعنوان: " نماذج من الوسطية في حياة السلف"، أكد فيها الشيخ - حفظه الله - أن الوسطية هي المنهج المستقيم والصراط العدل الذي جاء به رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من عند الله وهو خالٍ من الإفراط والتفريط ، وقال إن هذا المنهج الوسط السوي هو صراط الذين أنعم الله عليهم وسلكه السلف الصالح وتفاوتوا في سلوكه كتفاوتهم على الصراط الأخروي يوم القيامة ولكن جمهورهم وعمومهم سلكوا الوسطية في أعمالهم . واستشهد الشيخ الددو في هذا الموضوع بعدد من نماذج السلف الصالح ممن كانت الوسطية منهج حياتهم وتعاملهم وأولهم - كما ذكر - رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، حيث كان ينهج المنهج الوسطي في كافة أموره ، فكان فيما يتعلق بعلاقته مع الله عز وجل لا ينشغل بأمر الآخرة عن أمر الدنيا ولا ينشغل بالعبادة عن حقوق الآدميين إضافة إلى تعاملاته عليه الصلاة والسلام مع زوجاته والصحابة رضي الله عنهم وكذلك أخذه للنافع من حضارات الأمم الأخرى وعلومها كفكرة الخندق من حضارة فارس والخاتم من الروم والمنبر من الحبشة ، و ذكر الشيخ الددو أن أبا بكر الصديق كان نموذجاً آخراً لوسطية السلف الصالح وقال أنه بالرغم من رقة قلبه التي عُرفت عنه إلاّ أنه كان قوياً في الحق وهو الذي وقف في وجه الردة وكان صاحب سياسة يختار منها ما بتناسب مع الوقت ومقتضيات العصر ومن وسطيته أيضاً ما يتعلق بترتيب كتابة القرآن الكريم بعد موت 500 قارئ بواقعة اليمامة وسنته بالخلافة ، إضافة إلى وسطية عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه وذكر أنه كان وسطياً حتى أنه إذا تقدم بنهي للناس عن أمر بدأ بأهل بيته. ونشير هنا أن هذا المؤتمر خرج بتوصيات ونتائج من أهمها ما يلي: 1- دعوة الجامعات العربية والإسلامية إلى العناية في خططها وبرامجها بوسطية الإسلام من خلال تضمين مناهج الثقافة الإسلامية والعلوم الاجتماعية والتاريخية والتربوية والحضارية صوراً جليلة وناصعة لسيرة نبينا محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ، وقادة الأمة وأئمة العلم في عصورها الزاهية . 2- إبراز وسطية الإسلام في علاقة شباب الأمة وناشئتها بولاة أمرهم وطاعتهم في المعروف , وسماحته في علاقة المسلمين مع غيرهم . 3- اعتماد الحوار أسلوباً رئيساً للتعليم ، وإشاعة أدبياته في التفكير والممارسة . 4- توجيه الشباب إلى ضرورة تواصلهم مع علماء الأمة الربانيين وتقديرهم ، وأخذ العلم عنهم . 5- تفعيل التواصل بين المؤسسات الجامعية العربية، وتبادل الخبرات في مجال الفكر والمعرفة والدعوة إلى الوسطية ، والحث على الاستمرار في إبرام مذكرات التفاهم والشراكات بينها. 6- عناية الحكومات العربية بالوضع الاقتصادي للشباب والإسهام في حل مشكلة الفقر والبطالة , وتوفير فرص العمل الكريم لهم. 7- إعادة النظر في مكونات المناهج الجامعية ( الأهداف ، والمحتوى ، والأنشطة)، لتكون أكثر تفاعلاً مع القضايا المعاصرة ، وأقدر على دعم نهج الوسطية في الفكر والسلوك ، والحدُّ من ظاهرة التطرف والانحلال. 8- توعية الشباب بكيفية التعامل مع وسائل الإعلام والاتصال المختلفة, ومواقع التواصل الاجتماعي ؛ للاستفادة من إيجابياتها والحد من سلبياتها . 9- حث الإعلام على الإسهام في نشر ثقافة الوسطية وإبرازُ مظاهرها فيما يعرضه من برامج مختلفة , والحدُّ من ظاهرة التطرف والانحلال . 10- دعوة الجامعات إلى إنشاء مراكزِ أبحاث وطنية تُعنى بدراسة مظاهر الغلو والتطرف والانحراف لدى الشباب, وتسعى لكشف الحاجات الأساسية لهم, إسهاماً في بناء الشخصية المعتدلة . 11- تأسيس مراكزِ إرشاد تربوي نفسي داخل الجامعات ؛ تتولى إرشاد الطلاب نفسياً وتربوياً واجتماعياً وتهيئتَهم للتكيف مع المجتمع ومؤسساته. هذه أبرز توصيات البيان الختامي للمؤتمر، وسينشر الموقع بإذن الله مشاركات الشيخ الددو في هذا المؤتمر قريبا.
body_en:
His eminence the erudite Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan Ould al-Dedew — head of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars and president of Abdullah ibn Yasin University — took part in a conference on "The Role of Arab Universities in Strengthening the Principle of Balance among Arab Youth", organised by Taibah University at the Meridien Hotel in Medina the Illuminated, held over the period 1–4 Rabiʿ al-Thani 1432 AH, corresponding to 6–9 March 2011 CE.

A large company of the scholars of the Muslim world took part in this conference, and the participation of Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew, head of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars, took the form of a lecture in the main session entitled "The Balance of Islam and its Effect on Thought and Conduct". Among the lectures and activities the Sheikh is holding within the university's halls is a special course commenting on the book al-Akhlaq wa-l-Siyar of Ibn Hazm, this being the second course in the study and exposition of this book.

His eminence also delivered, among the events accompanying the conference the university is holding in these days, a lecture entitled "Examples of Balance in the Lives of the Early Generations", in which the Sheikh — may God preserve him — affirmed that balance is the straight method and the just path which the Messenger of God — may God bless him and grant him peace — brought from God, and that it is free of both excess and neglect. He said that this sound middle method is the path of those upon whom God has bestowed favour, and that the righteous early generations followed it, differing among themselves in their following of it as they will differ upon the otherworldly path on the Day of Resurrection — but the majority and generality of them followed balance in their deeds.

Sheikh al-Dedew adduced on this subject a number of examples of the righteous early generations for whom balance was the method of their lives and their dealings — and the first of them, as he mentioned, is the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in that he followed the balanced method in all his affairs. With regard to his relationship with God, mighty and majestic, he did not let the affair of the hereafter occupy him away from the affair of this world, nor let worship occupy him away from the rights of human beings; besides which there were his dealings — upon him be blessings and peace — with his wives and with the Companions, may God be pleased with them; and likewise his taking of what was beneficial from the civilisations of other nations and their sciences, such as the idea of the trench from the civilisation of Persia, the seal from the Romans, and the pulpit from Abyssinia.

Sheikh al-Dedew mentioned that Abu Bakr al-Siddiq was another example of the balance of the righteous early generations, and said that despite the tenderness of heart known of him, he was strong in the truth, and he it was who stood against the apostasy; and that he was a man of policy, choosing from it what suited the time and the requirements of the age. Part of his balance also is what relates to arranging the writing down of the Noble Qur'an after the death of five hundred reciters in the incident of al-Yamamah, and his instituting the practice regarding the caliphate. To this he added the balance of Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, mentioning that he was so balanced that whenever he came forward to forbid people something, he began with his own household.

We note here that this conference issued recommendations and conclusions, the most important of them being the following:

1 — Calling upon Arab and Islamic universities to give attention, in their plans and programmes, to the balance of Islam, by including in the curricula of Islamic culture and of the social, historical, educational and civilisational sciences noble and unblemished images of the biography of our Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and of the leaders of the community and the imams of learning in its flourishing ages.

2 — Bringing out the balance of Islam in the relationship of the community's youth and its rising generation with those in authority over them, and their obedience to them in what is right; and its tolerance in the relationship of Muslims with others.

3 — Adopting dialogue as a principal method of teaching, and spreading its proprieties in thought and in practice.

4 — Directing young people to the necessity of keeping contact with the godly scholars of the community, esteeming them, and taking knowledge from them.

5 — Activating communication between Arab university institutions, and exchanging expertise in the field of thought, of knowledge and of calling to balance; and urging that memoranda of understanding and partnerships between them continue to be concluded.

6 — Arab governments giving attention to the economic condition of young people, contributing to solving the problem of poverty and unemployment, and providing them with opportunities of dignified work.

7 — Reconsidering the components of university curricula (objectives, content and activities), so that they may engage more with contemporary issues, be better able to support the method of balance in thought and conduct, and limit the phenomenon of extremism and of dissolution.

8 — Making young people aware of how to deal with the various means of media and communication and with social networking sites, so as to benefit from their positive aspects and limit their negative ones.

9 — Urging the media to contribute to spreading the culture of balance and to bringing out its manifestations in the various programmes they present, and to limit the phenomenon of extremism and of dissolution.

10 — Calling upon universities to establish national research centres concerned with studying the manifestations of excess, extremism and deviation among young people, and seeking to uncover their basic needs, as a contribution to building the moderate personality.

11 — Founding centres of educational and psychological guidance within universities, to undertake the guidance of students psychologically, educationally and socially, and to prepare them to adapt to society and its institutions.

These are the most prominent recommendations of the conference's closing statement. The site will, God willing, publish Sheikh al-Dedew's contributions to this conference shortly.

flags.context: the organising term of the conference, of the Sheikh's lecture, and of all eleven recommendations
flags.note: The term carries the whole record and no glossary entry exists for it. 'Moderation' is the commonest English rendering but imports a political colouring that 'wasaṭiyyah' does not have in the Arabic, where it derives from the Qur'anic 'middle community' and is opposed to excess and neglect — which is exactly how the summary defines it two paragraphs later. 'Balance' is used throughout for that reason, and consistently, so that a reviewer can substitute one word everywhere if the office prefers another. This term should be settled corpus-wide before publication.

flags.arabic: 2- إبراز وسطية الإسلام في علاقة شباب الأمة وناشئتها بولاة أمرهم وطاعتهم في المعروف
flags.context: the second recommendation of the conference's closing statement
options: translate the recommendation exactly and attribute it to the conference, not to the Sheikh
omit the recommendations as not being his words
flags.note: Editorially sensitive, and a question of attribution as much as of content. The eleven recommendations are the closing statement of a conference held in Saudi Arabia in March 2011, at which the Sheikh was one of a large number of participants; they are not his words, and nothing in the record says he drafted, endorsed or voted for them. The second recommendation, on youth obedience to those in authority, reads very differently in English from the political positions attributed to him in records 677 and 679 from the same weeks. The English attributes the recommendations to the conference throughout. They must never be presented as his.

flags.context: the number of Qur'an reciters killed at al-Yamamah, in the summary of the lecture
options: render the figure exactly as given and flag it
adjust it to the figure usually given in the sources
flags.note: The figure of five hundred reciters is higher than the figure usually given in the standard accounts of al-Yamamah, and this is a summariser's report of a spoken lecture, so the number may be his rather than the Sheikh's. Rendered exactly as served; style guide section 6 forbids silently adjusting it. A reviewer should check it against the recording before the figure is published.

flags.arabic: يختار منها ما بتناسب مع الوقت
flags.context: the description of Abu Bakr as a man of policy
flags.note: 'ما بتناسب' has a bāʾ where a yāʾ is required; a simple typing slip. Left as served in body_ar and read as intended in the English. The source also writes 'وقال أنه' where 'وقال إنه' is standard after qāla, and uses both Arabic comma forms inconsistently within the numbered list; all left as served.

translator_notes: A site news notice reporting a conference and two lectures, not a text by the Sheikh. There are three distinct layers of attribution in it and the English keeps them apart: the site editor's reporting, the summary of what the Sheikh said in his lecture, and the conference's own closing statement. None of the three may be quoted as his written words.
The dual dating (1–4 Rabiʿ al-Thani 1432 / 6–9 March 2011) is the source's own and is kept in both calendars.
'السلف الصالح' is rendered 'the righteous early generations' rather than left as 'the Salaf', which in English carries a modern movement's name that the Arabic here does not.

The closing sentence promises that the site will publish the Sheikh's contributions to the conference; if those were published, they may exist as separate records and would be primary material where this notice is not.
